purpose: Select control specialised for choosing many options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a MultiSelect sits next to other form fields without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Every option row carries a checkbox indicator (the `Checkbox` Azion UI component), optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<MultiSelectContent>`. Since spec v4 the trigger can also show the selection as removable chips (`variant="chips"`, capped by `chipLimit` with a `+N more` chip), take typed text to filter the options in place (`searchable`), offer an `Add "…"` row for a typed value that matches no option (`allowCustom`, emits `create`), and render its own loading, error and empty list states (`loading`, `error`, `emptyTitle`) — the same vocabulary as `combobox`. MultiSelect is the one multi-pick field (`Select` picks exactly one): `modelValue` is always an array and the indicator is always a checkbox. Aligned with Figma frame `3899:29362` (options panel). The trigger reuses the `Input`/`Select` trigger visuals.
useWhen: Use MultiSelect whenever the person picks several values from a list in a form field; the chosen ones show as a count or chips in the trigger. For two to five options that fit on screen use a Checkbox per option; to build a large subset with both sides visible use TransferList.
Choosing several values from a long list (regions, tags, permissions) in a compact field.
A filter whose selected values stay editable from the same dropdown.
Grouped options with icons or trailing tags, optionally with search.
Tagging a record with labels people pick or type (`variant="chips"` + `searchable` + `allowCustom`).
Options fetched from a server as the person types (`searchable`, `:filter="false"`, `@search`, `loading`, `error`).
avoidWhen: Only one value may be chosen → use `select`.
A labelled form field with helper/error text → put it inside a `field`.
A handful of options that fit on screen → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
The user builds a subset and needs the chosen and remaining items side by side → use `transfer-list`.
Free-form tags with no list of options to pick from → use `tag-editor`.
related: `field` — wraps this control with its label, description and error; it hands the trigger its id and state.
`transfer-list` — dual-list transfer for building larger subsets.
`checkbox` — the indicator every option row renders.
`combobox` — single-value field with typed text; `searchable`, `allowCustom`, `filter`, `loading` and `emptyTitle` share its meaning.
bestPractices: `modelValue` is always an array; start it as `[]`, never `null`.
Pass `displayValue` to summarise long selections (e.g. "3 regions") instead of a list that overflows the trigger.
Keep each option's `value` stable and unique; selection is matched by value.

Put a search input in the `search` slot and a create action in the `footer` slot of `MultiSelect.Content` — or set `searchable` (and `allowCustom`) to type in the trigger itself; do not combine the two.
With `variant="chips"`, set `chipLimit` when the field sits in a dense row; leave it `0` in a form so every chip wraps and stays removable.
`create` only reports the typed value: add the new option to your list and its value to the model in the handler.
For a server-side search, set `:filter="false"`, fetch on `search`, and drive `loading` and `error` from the request.
